title: Avoid advancing RNG when creating agg devices
description:
## Summary

This PR replaces RNG-based device naming (`sample()`) with `tempfile()`-based names so that creating agg devices no longer advances the global RNG state.

## Motivation

Device creation currently mutates `.Random.seed`, which can be surprising in reproducible workflows. This can also make whitespace semantically meaningful in downstream jupyter contexts, e.g., latest containerized `jupyter/datascience-notebook`. 

## Changes

- Use `basename(tempfile())` to generate unique device names without touching RNG state
- Add tests asserting that `agg_capture()` and `agg_record()` do not advance the global RNG

## Notes

- `tempfile()` does not create files and does not use or modify `.Random.seed`
- Behavior is unchanged except for the removal of RNG side effects during device creation

title: Add "Supported By Posit" badge to ragg website
description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the ragg website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

title: WebP animation support
description:
A sequel to https://github.com/r-lib/ragg/pull/195 (containing the same changes as it's based on that branch), this adds animation support within a WebP device. Frames are collected in-memory and stitched into an animation on dev.off(). Example:

```
agg_webp_anim("animation.webp", delay=100)
for(i in 1:10) {
  plot(sin(1:100 + i)) 
  dev.flush()
}
dev.off()
```

title: only draw fill with AA if stroke is drawn
description:
Fix #96 and fix #131

This is an attempt to address the issue of neighbouring rectangles having a thin line between them due to anti-aliasing. In the default devices this is handled by never drawing fill with AA, which is extremely heavy-handed and mainly just result in poor quality.

While the issue can arise from all types of polygons, it is most prevalent with axis-oriented rectangles (when it comes to data-viz). Thankfully this is also the case where turning off antialiasing does not result in poor image quality, but at most small imprecisions in the placement of the rectangle (exasperated by low resolution).

The fix proposed here will clip rectangles to the pixel grid (thus turning off AA) _if_ fill is drawn _but not_ stroke. It seems to me this will strike a good balance. It will probably make sense to also have a setting to turn it off, to revert to the old behaviour

title: Raster image incorrectly rendered
description:
Hi, from another thread (https://github.com/yixuan/showtext/issues/33#issuecomment-623023377) I found a potential bug of `ragg` for the raster device function. Below are some minimal examples to reproduce:

```r
mat = matrix(c("#FF000011", "#FF000066", "#FF0000AA", "#FF0000FF"), 2)
ras = as.raster(mat)

png("1.png", width = 200, height = 200)
par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
plot.new()
rasterImage(ras, xleft = 0, ybottom = 0, xright = 1, ytop = 1, interpolate = FALSE)
dev.off()

ragg::agg_png("2.png", width = 200, height = 200)
par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
plot.new()
rasterImage(ras, xleft = 0, ybottom = 0, xright = 1, ytop = 1, interpolate = FALSE)
dev.off()

ragg::agg_png("3.png", width = 200, height = 200, bitsize = 16)
par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
plot.new()
rasterImage(ras, xleft = 0, ybottom = 0, xright = 1, ytop = 1, interpolate = FALSE)
dev.off()
```
![1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/216398/80896742-908ca500-8cbf-11ea-9cca-578688d02d94.png)![2_org](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/216398/80896743-91bdd200-8cbf-11ea-9e37-88fea0def23f.png)![3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/216398/80896744-92566880-8cbf-11ea-87b0-702fe9ef94f6.png)

You can find that the second plot was incorrectly rendered.
The reason is that the raster data need to be converted to the proper type before passed to AGG, similar to the case of `AggDevice16`. This patch should fix this.

Add Sixel graphics device support
description:
This PR adds a new `agg_sixel()` graphics device to `ragg`, enabling R graphics to be rendered directly to the terminal using the SIXEL bitmap graphics protocol.

The output is written to standard output when the graphics device is closed with `dev.off()`. This allows plots to be displayed in terminal emulators that support SIXEL graphics.

## Implementation Details
- Add a new `agg_sixel()` graphics device.
- Implement a self-contained SIXEL encoder in a single header-only C++ file, without introducing external dependencies such as libsixel.
- Write the encoded graphics to standard output when the device is closed.
- Register and export the new device, with corresponding documentation.

## Usage

```r
agg_sixel()
plot(sin, -pi, 2 * pi)
dev.off()
```

The resulting SIXEL data is written to standard output and can be rendered by compatible terminal emulators.

## Output Handling
The SIXEL output is written directly to `stdout` using `fwrite()`, since it consists of terminal escape sequences and should ideally be interpreted by a terminal emulator rather than displayed as text in an R GUI console.

This triggers a `devtools::check()` NOTE about writing to `stdout` from compiled code. I'm not entirely sure whether there is a more appropriate R API for this use case, so I'd appreciate your advice on whether this approach is acceptable or if there is a better alternative.

## Testing
Verified on the following terminals:

|Platform|Terminal Emulator|Supports SIXEL<sup>1</sup>|Result|
|----|----|----|----|
|Windows|Windows Terminal|Yes|Succeeded|
|Windows|WezTerm<sup>2</sup>|Yes|Succeeded|
|Windows|VS Code<sup>3</sup>|Yes|Succeeded|
|Windows|Alacritty|No|Ignored|
|Ubuntu|Konsole|Yes|Succeeded|
|Ubuntu|WezTerm|Yes|Succeeded|
|Ubuntu|XTerm<sup>4</sup>|Yes|Succeeded|
|Ubuntu|GNOME Terminal|No|Ignored|
|Ubuntu|VS Code|Yes|Succeeded|

1. SIXEL support information is based on https://www.arewesixelyet.com/
2. Requires the Nightly build of WezTerm
3. The following options need to be enabled: `enableImages`, `gpuAcceleration`, and `windowsUseConptyDll` (only on Windows)
4. XTerm needs to be launched with `xterm -ti 340`
